views.label: Device assignment
views.note: Sync devices by cursor, then drive assignments from stored state.

views.label: Service authentication
views.note: dep uses OAuth 1.0a; axm uses OAuth access tokens; Apps and Books uses a location sToken; software lookup is public.

cards.title: Service authentication
items: The dep client uses OAuth 1.0a to obtain a session token, then sends X-ADM-Auth-Session on device-assignment requests.
axm exchanges an ES256-signed client assertion for an OAuth access token, then uses that token as Bearer authentication on API calls.
Software catalogue lookup uses public HTTPS requests; it does not use the device-assignment or business API credentials.
Apps and Books sends the original location sToken as a bearer credential and checks the returned library UID and MDM identity.
AxM serial-based helpers explicitly resolve the full organization list to returned opaque resource IDs before mutation. Ambiguous or missing serials and incomplete enumeration fail closed.

Activity CSV downloads allow the API origin and HTTPS store.blobstore.apple.com on port 443. Downloads use bounded GET retries, Retry-After, backoff and cancellation with sanitized retry logs. API downloads replay once after a 401. Storage gets no API bearer or cookies and never refreshes OAuth; redirects are rejected. Intended serial-set completeness and per-device success are checked separately with an explicit observed CSV schema.
Apple activity information — https://developer.apple.com/documentation/applebusinessapi/get-orgdeviceactivity-information
Explicit serial-to-resource resolution — https://github.com/deploymenttheory/go-apple-dm/blob/557c464864be88a7a2e60afa4cc6c6139e03e094/devicemanagement/appleplatformservices/axm/serials.go

cards.title: Independent collection and correlation
items: Explicit account-scoped assignment intent persists targets, acceptance, terminal CSV outcomes and separate linkage convergence. Every binding replacement has a new generation. Revoked authority retains the overlap lock for submitted work; uncertain submissions never issue another POST. Remote attempt expiry leaves worker-lifetime bookkeeping and sibling application workers running, while lease checks still reject stale commits.

Named-account API and CLI reads atomically snapshot connection metadata and sealed credentials per request, require explicit grants and audit access capture before contacting Apple, and withhold results until completion capture. Account incarnation, revision and credential checks fence replaced connections. Raw device and coverage evidence needs separate raw-inventory authority. Diagnostics distinguish authentication, permission, empty inventory and incomplete synchronization without returning upstream errors or secrets.
Named account operation routes — https://github.com/deploymenttheory/go-apple-dm/blob/95e35f66a8e5a82885e8cac5e593b45754836fc3/server/internal/app/adminaxmaccounts.go
The collection package emits raw organization-device, detail, assignment and coverage resources without importing inventory. Raw list documents retain included resources and unknown envelope fields.
The host selects streams and owns account credentials, scheduling, leases and an atomic evidence/outcome/checkpoint sink. Inventory synchronization composes the same collector.

A new collector resumes committed versioned checkpoints. Failures retain successful evidence; only an exhausted successful list stream emits completion. Completion does not promise an Apple-side snapshot.

Collector persistence and resumption — https://github.com/deploymenttheory/go-apple-dm/blob/557c464864be88a7a2e60afa4cc6c6139e03e094/devicemanagement/appleplatformservices/axm/collection/collection.go

Explicit correlation accepts an actual organization-device resource and authenticated matching serials for ADE, account-driven Device Enrollment or profile-based Device Enrollment. User Enrollment receives no serial-based hardware enrichment. Opaque IDs retain protocol addressing and provenance roles.

Optional resolution requires caller-declared equivalent meanings and units. Latest successful native field evidence wins before Apple regardless of Apple refresh time; omissions retain prior native reports, and originals and disagreements remain inspectable. Neither operation requires an inventory repository.
Standalone serial correlation and optional resolution — https://github.com/deploymenttheory/go-apple-dm/blob/57e67022f98e9df9b75863020fc466b7c8af596f/devicemanagement/correlation/correlation.go
Native-first equivalent-field resolution — https://github.com/deploymenttheory/go-apple-dm/blob/57e67022f98e9df9b75863020fc466b7c8af596f/devicemanagement/correlation/resolve.go

cards.title: Independent source evidence
items: Inventory retains one record per source kind, account and opaque identity. Successful original history, complete list documents and safe failed outcomes remain separate; original JSON bytes and numeric lexemes survive persistence. Selectors use data.<original path> and meta.<column>; original data.id and repository meta.id never shadow one another.

Explicit serial links retain both source identities without merging records or ranking fields. Newly retained originals, including delayed reports, invalidate affected links; exact replays retain checked links. Absence or disconnection requires a fresh correlation. Optional resolution stays caller-owned.

Migration retains opaque original source envelopes, derives reconstructed facts only from actual raw JSON, and leaves missing originals or authenticated enrollment provenance incomplete and refreshable. Normalized aliases cannot fabricate source values.

Old worker owners are fenced through the existing lease guard. Incompatible checkpoints restart under a new generation while the previous outbound lease deadline prevents overlapping Apple requests. Evidence and checkpoint writes remain atomic.
Independent source persistence — https://github.com/deploymenttheory/go-apple-dm/blob/840163310d08110feab368693b8a58c5f69c510f/devicemanagement/inventory/records.go

SQL migration and restore preserve an active retired-writer fence; MySQL installs only missing guard DDL and uses current locking reads. — https://github.com/deploymenttheory/go-apple-dm/blob/840163310d08110feab368693b8a58c5f69c510f/server/inventorystore/fence.go

cards.title: Inventory and assignments
items: Inventory pages and cursors commit atomically after account, credential and cursor checks. Only the final page of the current full-fetch generation reconciles missing devices; interrupted or superseded fetches cannot delete unseen inventory.

Sync and assignment run independently. Assignment outcomes and readback recheck lease ownership, Apple account identity, OAuth credentials and the desired profile before saving; a conflict stops that run.
Apps and Books returns asynchronous event IDs. The caller persists progress, authenticates notifications and checks completion before installation.

Apps and Books preserves finite/sentinel and unlimited asset arrays plus original JSON. Optional counts distinguish missing from zero; totalCount 2147483647 means unlimited. Bounded traversal retains the location filter; stock does not establish licensing, dispatch or installation.

cards.title: DEP renewal, reset and cooldowns
items: Ordinary token imports reject established Apple identity or consumer-key changes. Force permits an atomic identity reset only with a validated server UUID; same-identity renewals preserve inventory and local settings.

Old responses cannot restore reset inventory or sessions. A still-owned lease may retain HTTP 429 or device THROTTLED cooldowns across a same-identity token or desired-profile change; identity reset discards the old server’s cooldowns.
Local checks cannot undo requests already accepted by Apple. Later reconciliation reads current Apple state.
Token validation and atomic reset — https://github.com/deploymenttheory/go-apple-dm/blob/557c464864be88a7a2e60afa4cc6c6139e03e094/devicemanagement/appleplatformservices/dep/token.go

cards.title: Software updates
items: The enrollment handler applies its configured update policy. Software lookup supplies available versions; it does not itself send the device’s HTTP rejection.
